cases.finding: The live tau2 integration directly instantiates an ordinary success claim, complementary post-condition access to actual environment state, discrepancy detection and in-flight corrective feedback. The audited system is the composed agent plus TrueCall layer rather than a canonical Index harness.

SWE-Review-Bench directly closes a complementary audit loop at its benchmark-defined boundary: a separate reviewer agent explores the repository and candidate PR, produces an approve/reject verdict plus structured discrepancy feedback, rejected work returns to the original PR generator for correction, and the revised patch is re-verified through SWE-bench. Published iterative review-revision improves downstream resolve rate, including a reported Qwen3-30B-A3B path from 27.5% to 56.9%. The reviewer/revision/verification organization is benchmark-defined, so these results are composed direct S3* evidence rather than native S3* evidence for OpenHands, Harbor, Claude Code, Codex Guardian, or any PR-generator harness.

harness-bench Pilot 4 directly closes a benchmark-defined complementary audit loop: an adversarial reviewer independently challenges the producer diff, two published L2 FULL runs return REQUEST_CHANGES findings into the original executor session, both execute a revision, and build plus visible and held-out verification pass afterward. The benchmark explicitly uses a clean-room harness rather than production Telos code, so this is composed direct S3* evidence and not native evidence for Telos, Claude Code, or another canonical harness.

SWE-agent's first-party benchmark configuration runs RetryAgent with multiple attempts and a distinct chooser/reviewer, so its native S3* mechanism is genuinely exercised. SWE-bench scores end-to-end software-task success rather than complementary-audit discrepancy and feedback, so this remains native proxy evidence rather than direct S3* evidence.

Canonical Codex already has a first-party Guardian S3* constructor path, but TrueCall wrapping adds a separate external post-condition audit layer. A TrueCall-wrapped Codex run would therefore measure the composed system unless a benchmark explicitly exercises Codex Guardian itself.

AuditBench provides alternative investigator access to hidden target-model behavior, but the target is an external benchmark object and findings need not return into current control of the same operating organization. It remains a strong S3* proxy rather than a direct same-system closure benchmark.

HarnessAudit-Bench provides strong trajectory-level evidence over 210 tasks by externally auditing boundary compliance, execution fidelity and system stability across multiple harness/framework configurations. That external audit can expose unauthorized resource access and inter-agent information-flow violations, but the published evaluation does not establish a native complementary S3* path that returns detected discrepancies into the same harness's current-control loop for correction and re-verification. It is therefore valuable S3* proxy/scaffolded evidence rather than a direct canonical S3* observation.

SilentProbe supplies a strong negative control for the S3* independence boundary. It exposes ordinary tool-using agents to production-API silent failures and reports that models detect the resulting failure in only 12% of full-loop cases and repair it in 0%. The addressed risk is S3*-relevant claim-vs-reality mismatch, but the evaluated mechanism is the same agent reasoning over its own operational path rather than a materially distinct complementary evidence channel with independent access, corrective return into current control and re-verification. The measurements therefore remain non-direct scaffolded evidence and must not be interpreted as a canonical S3* capability score.

PawBench publishes a Self_Verification capability slice, but the slice remains task-performance evidence. Its label does not establish a materially distinct complementary evidence path, audit independence, claim-vs-reality discrepancy detection, corrective return into current control, or re-verification. It must not be mapped to VSM S3* by vocabulary similarity.

cases.benchmark: Codex Guardian / AutoReview native audit path
cases.finding: Codex has a real first-party Guardian/AutoReview constructor path with separate review and structured allow/deny return into execution. The reviewed public search did not recover a first-party published benchmark cell that directly measures this native complementary-audit path under a matched canonical-harness comparison. Preserve the missing benchmark as a gap rather than assigning a score from external wrappers or generic review claims.

Omnigent's bundled Polly organization has a separate cross-vendor reviewer whose blocking findings become corrective fix tasks, so the native path satisfies the structural S3* boundary. The reviewed benchmark surfaces did not provide published reviewer-specific discrepancy, corrective-return and re-verification results under a matched canonical-harness design; generic release or performance regression benchmarks therefore do not close the S3* primary gap.

thClaws Team mode has a native complementary audit path: a teammate completion claim can be challenged through direct lead inspection of workspace state and failed work can be returned to the responsible teammate for correction. The reviewed repository search did not recover a published benchmark exercising this exact claim-to-inspection-to-corrective-return path, so no direct canonical S3* observation is admitted.

Reigen/Conductor supplies a constructor-level complementary verification path in which a project-configured verification command inspects a finished child's worktree before the manager consumes the completion event and the verdict returns into current control. The reviewed public search did not recover a published direct benchmark of that native verification constructor, so the canonical direct registry remains empty.

Canonical redteam establishes S3*=A in its default agent-pair path: a fresh cross-provider reviewer independently inspects the committed implementation diff and project constraints, CHANGES_REQUESTED findings are returned to the implementer, and review runs again before draft-PR creation. The pinned repository includes benchmark machinery but no committed real Phase-1 result set was recovered, so this is native mechanism-only coverage and no direct canonical capability observation is admitted.

Canonical AppliedScientist establishes S3*=A through its separate fresh Reviewer service and Scientist correction/re-review loop. The first-party publication directly evaluates this organization over 30 scientific-revision trajectories and reports 128/150 execution-related weaknesses resolved (85.3%) while only 2/18 idea-related weaknesses are resolved (11.1%). This is admitted native direct S3* evidence; the result is first-party-reported rather than independently reproduced at the pinned Git revision and does not supply a matched cross-harness primary cell.

Canonical data-to-paper establishes S3*=A through a separate reviewer conversation whose findings return to the performer for revision. The first-party publication Figure 2B / Supplementary Run A5 directly shows that reviewer-to-revision closure. The evidence is descriptive-only and reports no aggregate S3*-specific score, so it is admitted as a native direct observation without creating a matched primary cell.
